4.17.10.en: Even the angels, though they are holy beings, are not entrusted with the mysteries of God, but God reveals them to whom He wills. God is the good Shepherd who tends His vineyard Himself; He does not hand over His affairs entirely into the hands of those in heaven or on earth, however great their purity or holiness. For the angels, if compared with God, are counted foolish, and if compared with His wisdom, are counted ignorant.

4.17.11.en: * There is no need to tell how, when Moses and Aaron disobeyed the command of God at the waters of Meribah, they did not enter the Promised Land (Num 13:10); for the blessed Job relates that the angels and every creature can err [(Job 18:4) - the speaker is Eliphaz).

4.18.0.en: St. Jerome How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed like the moth? [19]

4.18.1.en: By comparing the wisdom of the angels with the wisdom of God, the former is counted folly, and by comparing the life of earthly man with the life of the angels, the latter is counted as a moth.

4.18.2.en: If this is so for the angels who dwell in heaven, what then of men, who dwell in houses of clay? Perhaps by houses he means here the bodies that were created from dust. The angels do not die, whereas men are crushed like the moth between the fingers of the hand, easily and quickly. If God does not entrust His angels who dwell with Him in heaven, pure and immortal spirits, would He entrust man, who dwells on the earth, created from dust, and who dies for the most trivial causes as the moth is crushed?

4.18.3.en: * We dwell in houses of clay, since we exist in earthly bodies. Paul, reflecting well on this, said: "But we have this treasure in earthen vessels," and also: "For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have in the heavens a building of God, an house not made with hands" (2 Cor 4:7; 5:1).

4.18.5.en: * It is clear that God does not entrust the righteous as you trust in yourself, for God knows their nature and the inclination of their bodies to fall. The fallen angels drive (God) to refuse trust, since He perceives their corruption in them. He stripped them of their original dignity and rank, and made them debased, because they thought evil against Him. If this is so for those who have this nature and dwelt on high among the virtuous powers, if this is the case with the angels, whose nature is higher than ours, what shall we say of the others, of men who are still sinners? Their nature is not only dust, and their dwellings among the creatures are made of clay (Gen 2:7); these easily corrupt as sinners, like a garment eaten by the moth (Jas 5:2).

4.19.0.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it [20].

4.19.1.en: Man has no right to boast against God, nor to think that he possesses knowledge, for perhaps between morning and evening, before the day passes, a man dies and is no longer found on the earth. Every day, indeed every minute, people die on the face of the earth, and yet no one thinks of his own death; there is none who heeds this truth, nor any who is admonished in earnest.

4.19.2.en: * The sinner is cut off from morning to evening, that is, from the beginning of his life to its end he is wounded by committing sin... On the contrary, Paul rightly urges us, saying: "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil" (Eph 16:5). We redeem the time if with tears we mend our past life, which we lost through carelessness.

4.19.4.en: Is not their tent-cord plucked up from them? (the ropes of their tents)

4.20.1.en: Their human wisdom, in which they take pride, is taken away from them, and they die, and with them die their wisdom and their foolish plans.

4.20.2.en: *Eliphaz brings an accusation against all sinners in general, and was not ashamed to number Job among them.

4.20.3.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * As if he were saying: Those of whom you said, "without understanding they perish for ever" - these surely die without wisdom... Since the wicked look upon the chosen in a debased way, because they are walking toward an unseen life through visible death, it is therefore well said here: "They die without wisdom".. And because Eliphaz said these things, which are true in their meaning and are against the wicked, yet he was counted by the blessed Job as deserving of blame, and exalted himself in haughtiness over wisdom.

4.20.5.en: This is what man reached because of sin, but the Incarnation of the divine Word and the offering of salvation changed the situation completely.

4.20.6.en: * We obtained this because of the "body" which the Lord offered; He offered to the Father the firstfruits of our nature. And because of the dignity of the One who offered and the perfection of the offering, the Father found the "gift" acceptable, received it with His hand, joined it to Himself, and said (to the incarnate Lord): "Sit thou at my right hand" (Ps 110:1).

4.20.7.en: Did not (the humanity united with the divinity) rise above the heavens?!

4.20.8.en: Is this not an honor beyond measure?!

4.20.9.en: Our nature (in the person of the incarnate God) has risen above the heavens, and has been exalted above the angels. It has passed over the archangels and the Cherubim, and soared above the Seraphim, higher than all the heavenly powers, and has rested in the true divine throne alone...

4.20.10.en: The conduct of our race was so evil in the past that it was in danger of the whole human race being wiped from the face of the earth. And now we, who were formerly counted unworthy to remain on the earth, have been raised to the heavens.

4.20.11.en: We, who were formerly unworthy of earthly glory, now ascend to the Kingdom of Heaven, and enter the heavens, and take our place before the divine throne.

4.20.12.en: This nature of ours, from which the Cherubim guarded the gates of Paradise, behold, today it is raised above the Cherubim!

4.20.13.en: How can we pass over so great an event (the Feast of the Ascension) so quickly?!

4.20.14.en: For we who have wronged such great mercies, so that we became unworthy of the very earth, and fell from all authority and dignity - by what merit are we raised to such a high honor?!

4.20.17.en: For this is truly wonderful: that peace has come, not through any work done by those who provoked God's wrath... but He who was rightly angry with us Himself calls us to peace. For the Apostle says: "Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us" (2 Cor 20:5). And what does this mean? That although we have wronged Him, it is He who seeks us and calls us to peace. It is truly so, for since He is God, and the God who loves, He calls us to Himself.

4.20.18.en: St. John Chrysostom * He who knows the weakness of human nature gains experience of the power of God.

4.20.19.en: Father Maximus the Confessor * When you hear that the divine majesty is higher than the heavens, that its glory cannot be expressed, its beauty cannot be described, and its nature cannot be approached, do not despair of seeing what you desire. It is within your power, for within you is the capacity by which you can perceive divine things. For He who created you gave you at the same time this wonderful loftiness.

4.20.21.en: Anoint my words with the anointing of love!

4.20.22.en: * Job's friends set it in their hearts to crush him!

4.20.23.en: They thought the bitter moments of his calamities a favorable opportunity to attack him!

4.20.24.en: But let the whole world attack him; what can harm him, as long as You are on his side!

4.20.25.en: What can dishonor him, as long as You bear witness to him!

4.20.26.en: * Often I think myself wise, and count my words true.

4.20.27.en: But what is the use of understanding and wisdom without love?

4.20.28.en: Anoint my lips with the anointing of Your Holy Spirit, and set a guard over my mouth, that I may speak only what my heart carries of the overflow of Your love!

4.20.29.en: That I may love You, and so love Your creation, and instead of biting criticism fill every soul with hope in You!

4.20.30.en: * Eliphaz saw in righteous Job a hypocritical man; the unbearable calamities that befell him are the natural fruit of his hidden sins.

4.20.31.en: Job was counted wise in the eyes of men, teaching others and guiding them, yet he sees him unable to guide himself.

4.20.32.en: He sees him as a man unable to carry out what he recommends!

4.20.33.en: * Grant me holy eyes, that I may not look with the eyes of Eliphaz, filled with malice and lying in wait for his righteous brother, to bring false accusations against him!

4.20.34.en: * Grant me eyes compassionate toward my brethren, that my heart may cry within me:

4.20.35.en: Who is weak, and I am not weak?

4.20.36.en: Who is offended, and I burn not?

4.20.37.en: * In tender fatherhood Job did not know authority, and was not the one who commands and forbids those under his authority, but in tender fatherhood he guided many.

4.20.38.en: Nothing occupied him all the days of his life but the salvation of every soul, even the members of his household!

4.20.39.en: He was a support for the weak, strengthening their slack hands, raising them from their fall, and making firm the trembling knees!

4.20.40.en: He bore Your image, O Lover of mankind!

4.20.41.en: And he refused to work except according to Your divine good pleasure!

4.20.42.en: * Trials surrounded him to swallow him up, and sudden disasters followed one another without mercy, and Job seemed as one who had lost everything, even his health!

4.20.43.en: But as a man he cried to You in bitter groans, yet his heart did not turn aside, and his lips did not utter a word of blasphemy.

4.20.44.en: He counted that he had lost nothing, for You are his treasure, and the source of his goodness and his good things!

4.20.45.en: He lost nothing, for he had gained You!

4.20.46.en: * Eliphaz found his opportunity, and displayed his wisdom and his theological understanding.

4.20.47.en: He said: No righteous man suffers what has befallen Job, nor is any upright man destroyed as he has been destroyed!

4.20.48.en: This is nothing but a divine testimony to Job's hidden wickedness!

4.20.49.en: And since what befell him has befallen no one in all of history, he is the most wicked of the wicked, and the chief of all sinners and hypocrites.

4.20.50.en: Look at Job, like a lion that used to prowl, terrifying and threatening, and behold, now he is dying of hunger, with no prey.

4.20.51.en: He lost all his sons; he no longer has a cub!

4.20.52.en: The lion became the mockery of children, and a plaything with no power!

4.20.53.en: * Eliphaz saw a heavenly vision, and instead of being restrained, he trembled and feared, and went back to affirm that Job is not more righteous than the angels, for God charges His angels with folly!

4.20.54.en: Who is Job, dust and ashes, that he should justify himself before God!

4.20.55.en: Behold, his tent has been plucked up, and his death has become a disgrace and shame before all!

4.20.56.en: * In longsuffering God left Eliphaz and his friends to mock, and in His heavenly wisdom permitted Job to be insulted by them.

4.20.57.en: But behold, the insult becomes for him a store of earthly and heavenly glory.

4.20.58.en: And every accusation against him is turned into an eternal crown!

4.20.59.en: Let the wicked accuse the children of God unjustly, but He will not allow their rod to rest upon His righteous ones!

4.20.60.en: * Truly, no creature will be justified before You!

4.20.61.en: You alone are the Holy One!

4.20.62.en: Before the light of Your splendor, all lights vanish!

4.20.63.en: Before Your righteousness, no creature will be justified!

4.20.64.en: * If You, the Judge, came to save and not to judge, how dare I judge my brother?

4.20.65.en: How shall I rob You of Your throne, O Searcher of hearts?

4.20.66.en: Grant me, along with wisdom, love, and along with my longing for the salvation of all, a compassionate heart!

5.0.s.en: 1. The saints are witnesses to the wisdom of God

5.0.0.en: Call now, is there any that will answer thee?

5.0.1.en: And to which of the saints wilt thou turn? [1]

5.0.2.en: Eliphaz was very confident of his position, so he set before Job to choose the arbitrators. He says to him: "Call now, is there any that will answer thee?" meaning: search yourself throughout the whole world, is there anyone whom calamities have reached as they have reached you?

5.0.3.en: Is there a saint among all humanity to whom what befell you has befallen? God has not dealt with any saint in this way, so surely you are not one of them.

5.0.4.en: Is there among the saints one who cursed the day of his birth as you did?

5.0.5.en: Has any saint risen up in revolt as you did, and been so hasty in judgment?

5.0.6.en: "To which of the saints wilt thou turn?" They all agree with me in my opinion. All of them stand on my side, and support what I say.

5.0.7.en: Eliphaz spoke these words, counting Job deserving of blame. He was puffed up with the pride of wisdom.

5.0.8.en: * "And to which of the saints wilt thou turn?" He says this in mockery: you cannot secure the saints to support you in your affliction, those whom you did not want to be in your company when you were able.

5.0.10.en: * "Call now, is there any that will answer thee? and which of the holy angels dost thou behold?" (LXX) As if Eliphaz were saying: You amuse yourself when you think that God is a witness with you, while you are unable to enjoy a visit of an angel to you in your prayers. You met a deceiver who deceived you, and persuaded you that he was sent from God. He made you believe this, but it is clear that God has not given testimony to that for you.

5.0.11.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem As for the effectiveness of the prayers of the saints, it is said in the Book of Acts that an angel appeared in a vision to St. Paul and said to him: "Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee" (Acts 27:24).

5.0.12.en: * If here a ship in danger, suffering from foundering, was found, and the prisoners were saved for Paul's sake (Acts 27:24), consider what it will be for the holy person in his house; for many are the trials that assail us, trials more dangerous than the trials of nature, but God is able to grant us to be saved if only we obey the saints as those in the ship did, if we carry out what they command us. For they were not only saved, but also contributed to the faith of others.

5.0.13.en: While the saint was in chains he did greater works than those who are free.

5.0.14.en: Behold, the situation here is this: the free centurion needed his bound prisoner, the skilled captain of the ship was in want of one who was not a captain, but rather he was the true captain. For he steered, as a captain, a ship not of this kind (an earthly one) but the Church of the whole world, having learned from Him who is also the Lord of the sea. He steered it not by human skill, but by the wisdom of the Spirit. In this ship there are many shipwrecks, many waves, evil spirits, "without were fightings, within were fears" (2 Cor 7:5); and he was the true captain.

5.0.15.en: * Urge those who have friendly converse with God to offer more prayers, with greater perseverance, that the storm which is shattering the whole world may be calmed.

5.0.16.en: St. John Chrysostom * The world continues to exist only because of the prayers offered by Christians.

5.0.17.en: Aristides of Athens * Our prayers are common and public; when we pray we do not pray for one person, but for all the people, because we all, the whole people, are one.

5.0.18.en: * May the prayers for the brothers and sisters not cease in the presence of the Father's mercies.

5.1.0.en: 2 For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one. 3 I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation. 4 His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them. 5 Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the thirsty swalloweth up their substance.

5.1.1.en: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one [2].

5.1.2.en: Sinners are counted fools, since they do not accept God's wisdom. These are killed by anger, and envy corrupts their bones. Perhaps Eliphaz means by this that what befalls Job is the natural fruit of his foolishness, ascribing to him folly and stupidity.

5.1.3.en: He says that the deceiver deceived him and stirred up anger in him, and that he mocked him so that Job would kill himself. In this he wishes to justify himself, but his own stupidity has been revealed.

5.1.4.en: * [Wrath kills the fool, and envy slays the child] (cf. Job 2:5). It must be noted that he who is angry is a fool, and he who envies is counted a child. For the former is not without reason declared a fool, since he brings death upon himself by his own will, and lets himself be stirred up by anger. And the latter proves by his envy that he is an immature child, for when he is envious he testifies that the one he was able to torment is greater than he.

5.1.5.en: St. John Cassian * Nothing surpasses love, and consequently nothing is lower than anger. We must care for nothing, however useful and necessary it may seem, so as to avoid anger, which causes disturbance, and we must not be troubled by matters, even those we reckon to be non-essential, so that we may keep the calm of love and peace without lack, for we must realize that nothing is so destructive as anger and vexation, and nothing so profitable as love.

5.1.6.en: Father Joseph * Nothing is more dangerous than rage, nor harsher than anger!

5.1.7.en: * There is a drunkenness of anger more dangerous than the drunkenness of wine!

5.1.8.en: St. John Chrysostom * Let us consider how grave is the sin of anger (wrath), by which we are separated from tenderness, and the likeness to the image of the Most High is corrupted.

5.1.9.en: By anger wisdom is driven out, and we remain in folly in all that we do and are bound to do, as it is written: "Anger resteth in the bosom of fools" (Eccl 7:9). For with the withdrawal of the light of understanding, agitation corrupts the mind.

5.1.10.en: By anger life is lost, even wisdom appears held back. As it is written: [Wrath destroys the wise] (Prov 1:15) LXX...

5.1.11.en: By anger righteousness is nullified, as it is written: "For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God" (Jas 20:1)...

5.1.12.en: He who does not control his feelings with the prudence proper to man must live in solitude like an animal.

5.1.13.en: By anger harmony is destroyed, as it is written: "A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife" (Prov 15:18)...

5.1.14.en: By anger the light of truth is lost. As it is written: "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath" (Eph 26:4). For anger brings the darkness of confusion. God hides from him the rays of the knowledge of Himself. By anger the radiance of the Holy Spirit is shut off. On the other hand, it is written according to an ancient translation: "On whom shall my Spirit rest, but on him who is humble and peaceable and who trembles at my words" (Isa 2:66).

5.1.16.en: * If a person is angry as a human being, he puts an end to anger as a Christian.

5.1.17.en: St. Jerome * Whoever is irascible is devoid of longsuffering and love; he is quickly troubled by trivial words, and stirs up strife over some slight, petty matter, and wherever there is no place for him he throws himself in... Who does not mourn for such a one? He is abhorred by God and men.

5.1.18.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian * The Holy Spirit is called the peace of the Spirit, and anger is called the disquiet of the soul, so we must conclude that nothing keeps away from us the presence (work) of the Spirit like anger.

5.1.19.en: St. John Climacus It is not strange that Eliphaz accuses Job of jealousy or envy, which are Eliphaz's own sins, for he projects his faults upon him, saying: "and envy slayeth the silly one" [2].

5.1.20.en: * The envious man does not count the calamities that befall him a trial; rather the trial for him is the good that befalls another, and conversely success for him is not that he himself be happy, but that trials befall another. The envious man grieves at seeing the good deeds of people, and rejoices in the calamities that befall them. It is said that the birds of prey that devour dead carcasses are destroyed by a sweet fragrance (perfume), for their nature agrees with what is evil and corrupt. And anyone who comes under the control of this disease (envy) is destroyed by the happiness of his relatives and neighbors, but if he sees an evil temptation he flies to it and puts his crooked beak into it and brings out the hidden calamities.

5.1.21.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa *Before all things it befits the man upon whom the yoke is laid to be steadfast in his faith... let him drive away from himself envy and anger, and remove deceitful lips.

5.1.22.en: St. Aphrahat the Persian Sage * The harm is trivial and the danger slight when the limbs are wounded by a sword, for the healing is easy so long as the wound is visible and the remedy is applied. The sore that is seen can be treated easily. But the wounds of the envious are hidden and secret, and admit no cure for their healing, so they shut in upon themselves hidden pains within the recesses of the conscience.

5.1.23.en: * Such people do not enjoy food or take pleasure in drink. They are constantly groaning, sighing and grieving, for as long as envy is not driven out their hearts are torn day and night without ceasing.

5.1.24.en: All evils have limits, and every sin ends in the commission of the crime. The adulterer's sin ends at the limit of committing the transgression, the thief's crime stops when he kills, the robber puts a limit to his greed, and the deceiver puts an end to his fraud, but envy has no limits.

5.1.25.en: It is an evil that works continually, and a sin that has no end.

5.1.26.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr * [Envy kills the weak (the lesser - little one)] (cf. Job 5:2). It is impossible for us to envy anyone except those whom we think better than ourselves in a certain respect. Therefore it is said that envy kills the "lesser." For the envious man bears witness against himself that he is less than another, since envy torments him on his account...

5.1.27.en: Such was Cain, who went down to kill his brother, for he went mad when his offering was rejected, because of the one whose offering God accepted and who was preferred over him (Gen 4)...

5.1.28.en: And so Esau was inflamed to persecute his brother, because he lost the blessing of the birthright, being deprived of it for a mess of lentils (vegetables) (Gen 27:38; 29:25)...

5.1.29.en: And so the brothers sold Joseph to the passing Ishmaelites, since the secret of the revelation was hidden from them, and they put themselves in a position of opposition to his advancement, lest he be a ruler over them (Gen 5:37-11).

5.1.30.en: And so Saul persecuted his servant David by throwing a spear at him, for he feared that the man would attain a stature greater than his own, since he perceived his daily growth in virtue (1 Sam 10:18-11).

5.1.31.en: So the one whom envy kills is the weak (the lesser), for if he did not feel that he is the lesser he would not grieve at the goodness of others. For envy corrupts the mind and kills everything it finds good. Solomon said: "A calm (peaceful) heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones" (Prov 30:14)...

5.1.32.en: So whoever longs to be perfect and whole, let him avoid the poison of envy, and concentrate his affections on the inheritance which is not diminished by the number of heirs, which is one inheritance for all, and complete for each one. And which shows itself a greater inheritance the more the number of those who are granted it increases... So when a person does not long for evil things, nothing stands in the way of love.

5.2.0.en: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation [3].

5.2.1.en: Eliphaz sees that Job had previously taken root and prospered, but since he is foolish his state did not last. And behold, he curses his habitation. It is as though Eliphaz brings a new accusation against Job, for besides accusing him of hypocrisy, and that behind his seemingly good works he hides hidden evils that none knows but God, for which reason calamities unheard of in the history of mankind have befallen him, he was a fool who ran after wealth and the love of the world. An accusation as far as can be from the life of this righteous man!

5.2.2.en: Perhaps this does not mean that Eliphaz desired Job's destruction, but since he discovered - according to his thinking - that what befell him was from God's anger against him as a wicked man, he realized that it was by God's justice that Job should fall under the curse, to uproot him from this world with all his wealth, because his heart was attached to it.

5.2.3.en: Scripture warns us against loving the world and clinging to it. "Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world" (1 Jn 2:15-16). "Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God" (Jas 4:4).

5.2.4.en: * The foolish takes root in the earth and clings to it, for he is attached to the love of the earth with all the desire of his heart. He exalts himself by his rooting, when he clings in this world to temporal goods, until he obtains what he desires, and submits to no authority, and rules over the weak without resistance, and resists those who exercise authority well, and reaches better circumstances by wicked means, so that by leaving the true life, he lives this present time in greater happiness.

5.2.5.en: But when the weak see that the wicked prosper, they become fearful and troubled within, because of the scope that sinners have, and the steps of their mind stagger.

5.2.6.en: In the same way the psalmist declared: "But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped. For I was envious of the proud, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked" (Ps 2:73-3).

5.2.7.en: But when the strong see their glory, they immediately fix their minds on the punishment (discipline) that follows glory. And with deep inner thought of the heart they despise the things that swallow up the proud from outside with the increase of vain conceit. It is well said: "I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his beauty." For to curse the beauty of the fool is to condemn his glory by a considered judgment, for the more he sinks into torments the more he exalts himself in sin. For his arrogance is temporary, but his punishment is permanent.

5.2.8.en: He who begins his way with honor ends with judgment. In any case, the more the wicked man finds a way for himself in this world, the more people he draws into destruction, therefore it is rightly said: "His children are far from safety." For the children of the fool are those who imitate him, born in the ambition of this world. They are far from safety, especially as regards their practice of evil if compared with their freedom from weakness.

5.2.10.en: * You want now to inherit the earth; beware lest the earth inherit you.

5.2.11.en: If you are meek you inherit it, or if hard, it inherits you...

5.2.12.en: You will truly inherit the earth when you cling to the Maker of heaven and earth!

5.2.13.en: St. Augustine * Who that has tasted the sweetness of the fruits of the tree of life wants to run toward the foul fruits of (love of) the world?

5.2.14.en: * As fire does not stay in water, so the knowledge of God does not stay in a heart entangled with the passions of the world.

5.2.15.en: * None has perfectly renounced the world but he in whom Your fire burns always, O Lord.

5.2.16.en: St. John Saba * The soul that is about to receive the Word, the Logos, ought to die to the world (Gal 14:6) and be buried in Christ (Rom 4:6; Col 12:2), so that it finds none but Christ, for this is the fitting reception that He asks for Himself from it.

5.3.0.en: St. Ambrose His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them [4].

5.3.1.en: Perhaps the gate was high and fell on Job's children and those at the feast who thought themselves in peace and safety. It fell with its weight and crushed them beneath it, and there was none to deliver. So Job's evil - in Eliphaz's opinion - came upon his sons and destroyed them.

5.3.2.en: * This means: why are you terrified at the death of your children? For the children of fools do not perish because of lack of deliverance, but are afflicted while still alive... and there is no one to deliver them, since God requited them justly. Also their gain which they obtained unjustly is taken from them by the righteous, since there is none to save them from evil, and all their strength is wasted in pleasures and is exhausted, perishing by God's command.

5.3.3.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem Who are those who think they are safe, standing inside a house with a closed door, which none can break into to harm them? In Eliphaz's view, Job's sons and daughters, who in his opinion are wicked and hypocrites like their father, think themselves happy at the feast, and expect no harm to creep in upon them. They are safe, inside the gate, under the guard of their servants and slaves! But they are not safe; rather the gate, which is the source of their safety, falls on them and destroys them.

5.3.4.en: This saying bore a prophecy about the Lord Christ who said: "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture" (Jn 9:10). Through this door the Gentiles believed and entered into the faith, and went out to the heavenly life, and found divine pasture. This same door became a stumbling block to those who thought they were safe, since they clung to the letter of the Law, and thought that they, rather than others, were inside the divine doors.

5.3.5.en: They rejected faith in the Lord Christ, so the door - the entrance of believers - became a stumbling block to them, for He says: "If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloak for their sin" (Jn 22:15)

5.3.6.en: * Let us not be confused, brethren, in understanding Him, as He bears likenesses both as the door and also the doorkeeper. For what is the door? The way of entrance. Who is the doorkeeper? He who opens the door. Who then is He who opens it, but He Himself, where He reveals Himself to be seen?

5.3.7.en: * This great sin is their unbelief in Christ, who came specially to renew their faith. Had He not come, they would have been free of this sin.

5.3.8.en: By His coming the life of unbelievers became all the more laden with destruction, as it became for the salvation of those who believe. For He is the head of the Apostles and their chief, He became as they declared: [To some the savour of life unto life, and to some the savour of death unto death] (2 Cor 2:16).

5.3.9.en: St. Augustine * "And they are crushed in the gate..." As the entrance of a city is called a gate, so on the day of judgment it is the gate of the Kingdom, through which all the elect enter into the glory of their heavenly city... "Neither is there any to deliver them" [4]. For the Truth saves from eternal woe those who in their temporary state have been afflicted by discipline. He who refuses distress is left at that time without any means of salvation. For they did not care to receive Him (the Savior) as their Father who trains them, therefore the wicked in their time of trial will not find Him a deliverer who helps them.

5.3.11.en: * Now let us consider what the Gospels say in light of the promises of good things. And we must say: the good things that the Apostles proclaim in these Gospels are simply "Jesus."

5.3.12.en: One of the good things they proclaim is the resurrection. But the resurrection, in a certain sense, is Jesus, for He is the One who says: "I am the resurrection"...

5.3.13.en: As Isaiah says: [How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of those who bring good tidings of good] (Isa 7:52). He sees how beautiful and fitting is the proclamation of the Apostles who have walked (in Christ), and He is the One who says: "I am the way." He praises the feet of those walking in the way, those who think on Jesus Christ, and go through this door to God (the Father).

5.3.14.en: They proclaim the good things, the beautiful feet, that is, Jesus.

5.4.0.en: Origen Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the thirsty swalloweth up their substance [5].

5.4.1.en: Job's and his sons' wealth became plunder for the Sabeans and the Chaldeans. They broke through the barriers made of thorns, and seized the wealth.

5.4.2.en: Perhaps he refers here to the thief who steals the whole crop, even that mixed with thorns, or to the custom to which Dr. Thomson referred in his explanation of this passage, where he says that the farmers, after threshing the grain, often place it beside the straw in a special place, and cover it with thick bushes full of thorns so that the animals do not approach it and eat it, and when thieves want to steal the grain they must first remove these thorny bushes.

5.4.3.en: It says in the Jesuit translation (Dar al-Mashriq, Beirut): "The hungry eats his harvest, snatching it from among the thorns, and the thirsty swallows his wealth." He who does not open his heart with true inner love to the hungry, the thirsty and the needy becomes plunder for others. The hungry breaks into his storehouses, and the harvest is seized from among the thorns, and many thirst for his wealth, and count it their right to swallow all he has and leave him nothing.

5.4.4.en: Thus Eliphaz looks at Job and his children as not having been generous in love, but they gave generously for the sake of appearance and vain glory, while their hearts were dry and hard, so they deserved to have their possessions plundered by the hungry and thirsty.

5.4.5.en: In bitterness Tobit cried to the Lord, saying: [For we have sinned against You, and have not obeyed Your commandments, so You delivered us to plunder, and exile, and death, and we became a byword and a laughingstock and a reproach among all the nations among whom You scattered us] (Tob 3:4). And the psalmist says: "Thou makest us to turn back from the enemy: and they which hate us spoil for themselves. Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen. Thou sellest thy people for nought, and dost not increase thy wealth by their price... (Ps 10:44-14). And the Lord says: "Thy substance and thy treasures will I give to the spoil without price, and that for all thy sins, even in all thy borders" (Jer 13:15; cf. Jer 3:17; 6:30; 37:50; Ezek 21:7; 46:23; Isa 13:10).

5.4.6.en: * "Thy substance and thy treasures will I give to the spoil without price, but for all thy sins" (Jer 15:13). What are the riches of the sinners that God gives to the spoil in return for all their sins? Are they the riches that they gather on earth? Every man in fact lays up treasure for himself, either on earth if he is an evil man, or in heaven if he is a good man, as the Gospel tells us (Mt 19:6-20). Does He say to this people: because of your sins I give your treasures and riches to the spoil, meaning by those riches the prophets such as Jeremiah and Isaiah and Moses?! God has taken these treasures from this people, and said through the Lord Christ: "The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof" (Mt 43:21). This nation is we ourselves, for God has given the riches of this people (the prophets) to us.

5.4.7.en: They were first entrusted with the oracles of God (Rom 2:3), then we after them were entrusted with these oracles; they were taken from them and given to us. Likewise we can say that the statement: "The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof," which the Savior said, was fulfilled in Him. Not that Scripture was taken from them, but that they at present do not possess the Law nor the prophets, because they do not understand or grasp what is written in it. They have the books, therefore the kingdom of God that is taken from them is "the meaning of the Holy Scriptures." They do not care to know any exposition of the Law and the Prophets, but read it without understanding. And with the coming of the Lord the following prophecy was indeed fulfilled: "And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat" (Isa 9:6-10; Mt 14:13-15). The prophecy of Isaiah was also fulfilled: "For, behold, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water, the mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the diviner, and the ancient, the captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the skilful in enchantment" (Isa 1:3-3). All this God has taken from them, and given it to us who have come from the Gentiles...

5.4.8.en: He says: "Without price but for all thy sins, even in all thy borders," as though saying to this people: Your treasures and your riches I give to the spoil because of your sins that have filled all your borders, for there is no place among this people that is not filled with sin. How could all their borders not be filled with sins, they who killed the Truth, since the Lord Christ is the Truth, and killed Wisdom, since the Lord Christ is Wisdom, and killed Justice, since the Lord Christ is Justice? By judging the Son of God to death they lost all that truth, wisdom, and justice. And when the Lord of glory Jesus rose from the dead He never appeared to those who killed Him... but appeared only to those who believed in Him; He appeared to them alone when He rose from the dead.

5.4.9.en: "And I will make thee to pass with thine enemies (and subject thee to slavery in the midst of thine enemies) into a land which thou knowest not: for a fire is kindled in mine anger, which shall burn upon you"(a). This people has indeed been subjected to slavery in the midst of its enemies and in a land it did not know. And after these threatening words directed to the people, Jeremiah or the Lord Christ continues his prayer and adds to his previous words these words: "O LORD, thou knowest: remember me, and visit me, and revenge me of my persecutors; take me not away in thy longsuffering"(b) or [Be not longsuffering toward them](LXX).

5.5.0.en: 6 For affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth misery spring out of the ground, 7 but man is born unto toil, as the birds of prey to soar on the wing.

5.5.1.en: For affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth misery spring out of the ground [6].

5.5.2.en: After Eliphaz demonstrated that all Job lost is a just punishment from God, he began as one who encourages him lest he fall into despair.

5.5.3.en: "Affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth misery spring out of the ground." It is not like natural crops that sprout at certain times and come forth from the dust like grass, but all that happens is by divine providence. Or in other words: do not blame the soil when affliction appears, for it is not its doing, but yours, for the cause is within you. "If thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear it" (Prov 9:12).

5.5.4.en: As we do not expect trees to appear from soil without the planting of seeds, so it befits us not to think that afflictions come upon people without their having committed evils. What befell Job is not by chance, but is the harvest of evil planting.

5.5.5.en: This truth was revealed to us by our Lord Jesus, the Creator of the soul, who knows that the disease of the soul is in itself and not outside it. The human soul is like a single earthen vessel which differs only in the nature of what is inside it; if what is inside one is gasoline and inside another is water, the approach of a live coal will bring the first to burst into flames and explode, but the second will quench the coal.

5.5.6.en: St. John Chrysostom wrote more than one treatise affirming that no one and no circumstance can harm a person unless the person harms himself.

5.5.7.en: * Someone may say: Did not Satan harm Adam, since he corrupted his being, and made him lose Paradise?

5.5.8.en: For the cause here lies in the negligence of the one who was harmed, his lack of self-control, and his lack of striving. For Satan, who used various powerful schemes, could not subject Job to himself; how then could he, by lesser means, have dominated Adam, had Adam not been able by himself to master himself?!

5.5.9.en: What then? Does harm not befall one who is exposed to slanders and suffers the plundering of his property, so that he is deprived of his goods, driven out of his inheritance, and struggles in grievous poverty?

5.5.10.en: No, rather he benefits if he is dignified, for did these things harm the Apostles? Did they not always struggle with hunger, thirst and nakedness?! And because of these things they became glorified and renowned and gained for themselves more help from the Lord?!

5.5.11.en: And also what harm befell Lazarus because of his sickness and sores and poverty and having no one to shelter him? Were not these things weaving for him a crown of flowers of victory...?!

5.5.12.en: Joseph's brothers, for example, harmed Joseph, but Joseph himself was not harmed.

5.5.13.en: And Cain cast his nets for Abel, but Abel did not fall into them. And this is the reason for which disciplines and punishments exist.

5.5.14.en: For God does not lift the punishment from the one who devised the harm merely because of the good that the one who endured the harm enjoys, but confirms his punishment because of the evil of the doer of iniquity. For although those upon whom evil falls become more glorious at the expense of the plots devised against them, it was not in the intention of man that another should not harm him, but he gains great benefit at the hands of his adversaries.

5.6.0.en: St. John Chrysostom But man is born unto toil, as the birds of prey to soar on the wing [7].

5.6.1.en: Man was created to live in peace and rest and joy of heart, but by transgressing the commandment and turning his back on God, the source of his happiness, "man became born unto toil," for he was born in sin (Ps 51:5). And toil became as if an inseparable part of our being, or as if we were created to suffer it, as birds of prey were created to soar on their wings on high. It is not for us to be surprised at the affliction that befalls us as though a strange thing had happened to us (1 Pet 4:12). We must eat our bread in the sweat of our faces (Gen 3:19).

5.6.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that man's life is a continual striving with the enemy of good, entering a battle that does not stop, but these battles end in the victory of those who strive and their crown.

5.6.3.en: *He says: This despair springs from within people. Note how he was obliged once more to show that his words agree with nature, so that his speech would not be criticized. For human nature was created thus. For the earth produces nothing more pitiable than man, so it befits us not to be astonished or to wonder: we are born to cause pain and to suffer. This is also what the prophet said: "For all... the days of our years... yet is their strength labour and sorrow" (Ps 90:9-10). And Jacob said: [The days of the years of my life... few and evil] (Gen 9:47). "But man is born unto toil." He says that in our nature it is impossible to escape suffering. For he does not want anyone to object again that Job is righteous. He says: He is righteous, but human nature is usually created to endure evils. Note that he stepped out to nature to affirm that Job is not blameless.
